parts.title: Biotechnology’s Third Wave
parts.article:
A For most of its history, biotechnology was associated with medicine and agriculture. Its first wave brought drugs, vaccines and diagnostic tests; its second wave produced genetically modified crops and improved varieties of plants. A third wave, however, is now moving beyond hospitals and farms into factories, mines, paper mills and even clothing manufacturers. Instead of using heat, pressure and harsh chemicals to make products, this new form of biotechnology uses living systems, especially enzymes and microorganisms, to perform industrial tasks. Supporters argue that this change could be as important for manufacturing as steam power or electricity once were.

B The central agents in this third wave are enzymes, natural proteins that speed up chemical reactions. In the human body, enzymes help digest food, repair cells and release energy. In industry, the same basic principle can be used to break down starch, clean fibres, remove stains or convert plant material into useful substances. The advantage is that enzymes are highly specific: each one tends to perform only one type of reaction. This means that a factory can achieve a desired result with fewer unwanted by-products than traditional chemical processes usually produce.

C Enzymes are not new to industry. For decades, they have been added to washing powders to remove grease and protein stains at lower temperatures. They are also used in cheese-making, brewing and baking. What is new is the scale and precision with which they can now be designed. By studying the structure of natural enzymes and altering the genes of microorganisms, scientists can produce enzymes that remain active in unusual conditions, such as extreme acidity, high salt levels or relatively low temperatures. This has made them attractive to companies looking for cleaner and cheaper methods of production.

D One widely cited example is the textile industry. Traditionally, cotton fabrics were treated with strong chemicals to remove tiny loose fibres from the surface, a process that used large amounts of water and created chemical waste. Some manufacturers now use enzymes to perform the same task more gently. The fabric becomes smoother and brighter, while less water and energy are consumed. Enzymes are also used to fade denim jeans, replacing some of the stones and chemical bleaching agents once needed to create the popular worn look. For consumers, the final product may appear no different, but the method of production can be far less damaging.

E The paper and pulp industry has also experimented with enzyme-based processes. Wood pulp contains lignin, a tough material that must be removed or modified before paper can be whitened. Conventional bleaching can involve chlorine compounds, which may produce harmful pollutants if not carefully controlled. Certain enzymes can help loosen lignin or prepare the pulp for bleaching, reducing the amount of chlorine-based chemicals required. In other cases, enzymes help fibres drain more quickly, allowing paper machines to run faster and use less energy. These changes may sound minor, but in large factories even a small percentage saving can have significant economic value.

F A further development combines enzymes with genetic engineering. Instead of simply finding useful enzymes in nature, researchers can insert selected genes into bacteria, yeasts or fungi, turning them into miniature factories. These organisms can then produce large quantities of enzymes for commercial use. Some scientists are also designing microbes that can convert agricultural waste into biofuels, biodegradable plastics or industrial solvents. This combination of enzyme technology and genetic engineering is one reason the third wave is considered broader than earlier applications of biotechnology. It is not merely improving existing products; it is changing the way raw materials are processed.

G The commercial appeal is obvious, but it is not the only reason governments and companies are interested. Many countries are under pressure to reduce pollution, cut carbon emissions and use resources more efficiently. Industrial biotechnology can contribute to these goals because biological reactions often take place at lower temperatures and in water rather than in toxic solvents. As a result, factories may require less energy, produce less waste and rely less heavily on petroleum-based raw materials. However, critics warn that the environmental benefits are not automatic. Growing crops for bio-based products, for example, can compete with food production or lead to land-use problems if not managed carefully.

H Despite these concerns, many analysts believe the third wave could bring major environmental advantages. In theory, it offers a way to make industrial production cleaner without asking consumers to give up the goods they use every day. Detergents can work in cold water, jeans can be faded with fewer chemicals, paper can be bleached with less pollution, and fuels can be made from plant waste rather than crude oil. The promise is especially attractive because it links environmental protection with profit: companies save money while improving their public image. For this reason, biotechnology is increasingly viewed not just as a scientific field, but as a tool of sustainable commerce.

I There remain obstacles. New biological processes must be reliable, safe and cost-effective before manufacturers will adopt them. Customers may also be suspicious if they hear that genetic engineering is involved, even when the genetically modified organism is used only inside a factory and is not present in the final product. Regulation varies from country to country, and companies must prove that their methods do not create new risks. Nevertheless, the direction of travel is clear. The third wave of biotechnology is moving from the laboratory into everyday industry, and its influence may become visible not in what consumers buy, but in how those products are made.

Q17 a possible negative consequence of producing materials from biological resources

Questions 18-19
Choose TWO letters, A-E.

Q18 According to the passage, which TWO of the following are true about enzymes?

  • A They bring about changes without producing as many unwanted substances.
  • B They operate only inside the human body.
  • C They can be adapted to function in conditions that are not normally favourable.
  • D They remove the need for microorganisms in production.
  • E They make all industrial processes completely waste-free.

Q19 According to the passage, which TWO of the following are true about enzymes?

Questions 20-21
Choose TWO letters, A-E.

Q20 Which TWO of the following statements are true about the third wave of biotechnology?

  • A It has extended biotechnology into sectors beyond healthcare and farming.
  • B It has already replaced conventional manufacturing in most factories.
  • C It may allow some goods to be produced with lower environmental impact.
  • D It has made consumers more willing to accept genetic engineering.
  • E It depends mainly on the use of extreme heat and pressure.

Q21 Which TWO of the following statements are true about the third wave of biotechnology?

Questions 22-26
Complete the summary below.
Choose ONE WORD ONLY from the passage for each answer.
Industrial biotechnology may change the way everyday goods are produced, even when the finished items look the same to . In fabric treatment, biological agents can improve the appearance of cotton while cutting the need for water and . In paper production, they can help reduce reliance on chlorine-based . Some microbes can be turned into miniature by inserting selected genes into them. Before such methods are widely accepted, firms must demonstrate that they will not introduce new .

reference:
Q14

解析 D段直接拿纺织业举例，说明现在制造商用酶这种温和的方法，替代了以前用的强效化学品。

干扰 你可能会想选C段，因为里面提到了酶在工业上的新应用，但C段并没有给出一个具体的“传统制造工艺被替代”的例子。

句子 One widely cited example is the textile industry. Traditionally, cotton fabrics were treated with strong chemicals to remove tiny loose fibres from the surface, a process that used large amounts of water and created chemical waste. Some manufacturers now use enzymes to perform the same task more gently. The fabric becomes smoother and brighter, while less water and energy are consumed.

Q15

解析 H段点明了这种清洁生产方式把环保和利润绑在了一起，既能帮公司省钱，又能提升公众形象（改善商业地位）。

干扰 你可能看到E段提到了“经济价值”，但H段才真正把“清洁生产（环保）”和“改善商业地位（利润和形象）”完美对应了起来。

句子 The promise is especially attractive because it links environmental protection with profit: companies save money while improving their public image. For this reason, biotechnology is increasingly viewed not just as a scientific field, but as a tool of sustainable commerce.

Q16

解析 F段讲到研究人员把选定的基因植入细菌或真菌中，把这些生物体改造成能大量生产商业用酶的“微型工厂”。

干扰 你可能看到E段也讲了酶的作用，但只有F段明确指出了“改造生物体（植入基因）”来制造有用物质的过程。

句子 A further development combines enzymes with genetic engineering. Instead of simply finding useful enzymes in nature, researchers can insert selected genes into bacteria, yeasts or fungi, turning them into miniature factories. These organisms can then produce large quantities of enzymes for commercial use.

Q17

解析 G段指出了利用生物资源制造产品可能带来的负面后果，比如种农作物可能会和粮食生产抢夺土地资源。

干扰 你可能会误选I段，因为那里提到了“风险（risks）”，但I段讲的是消费者对基因工程的疑虑以及合规要求，真正指出“使用生物资源会产生负面环境后果”的是G段。

句子 However, critics warn that the environmental benefits are not automatic. Growing crops for bio-based products, for example, can compete with food production or lead to land-use problems if not managed carefully.

Q18

解析 A选项说酶产生的无用物质较少，完美对应B段中说明的：工厂使用酶可以达到预期效果，且产生的有害副产品比传统化学工艺更少。

干扰 你可能会选E觉得是完全无废物的，但原文只说了副产品“更少（fewer）”，并不是“完全没有（completely waste-free）”。

句子 The advantage is that enzymes are highly specific: each one tends to perform only one type of reaction. This means that a factory can achieve a desired result with fewer unwanted by-products than traditional chemical processes usually produce.

Q19

解析 C选项说酶能适应通常不利的环境，对应C段提到的：科学家可以制造出在极端酸性、高盐或低温等不寻常条件下依然保持活性的酶。

干扰 你可能会选B，但B段不仅说了酶在人体内起作用，还说了在工业中也能用，并不是“只（only）”在人体内运作。

句子 By studying the structure of natural enzymes and altering the genes of microorganisms, scientists can produce enzymes that remain active in unusual conditions, such as extreme acidity, high salt levels or relatively low temperatures.

Q20

解析 A选项说第三次浪潮把生物技术扩展到了医疗和农业之外，对应原文提到的第三次浪潮正走出医院（医疗）和农场（农业），进入工厂甚至服装制造商。

干扰 你可能会选B觉得它已经取代了传统制造业，但原文说的是“正在进入”，并没有说在大多数工厂“已经取代（already replaced）”。

句子 A third wave, however, is now moving beyond hospitals and farms into factories, mines, paper mills and even clothing manufacturers.

Q21

解析 C选项说它可以让一些商品在生产时降低环境影响，对应G段里提到的生物反应让工厂需要更少的能源，产生更少的废物。

干扰 你可能会被D选项迷惑，但原文在I段明确指出消费者对基因工程仍可能感到怀疑，并没有说他们“更愿意接受”。

句子 Industrial biotechnology can contribute to these goals because biological reactions often take place at lower temperatures and in water rather than in toxic solvents. As a result, factories may require less energy, produce less waste and rely less heavily on petroleum-based raw materials.

Q22

解析 D段指出，尽管生产方法变了，但对于消费者（consumers）来说，最终产品看起来并没有什么不同。

干扰 你可能会去苦找“look the same”的原词，但在原文中它被同义替换成了“appear no different”，直接锁定它前面的consumers就行。

句子 Enzymes are also used to fade denim jeans, replacing some of the stones and chemical bleaching agents once needed to create the popular worn look. For consumers, the final product may appear no different, but the method of production can be far less damaging.

Q23

解析 D段提到，用酶处理织物能让布料更平滑鲜亮，同时消耗更少的水和能源（energy）。

干扰 填空时你可能会顺手填成water，但题目里已经给出了water，你需要填的是原文中跟它并列的energy。

句子 Some manufacturers now use enzymes to perform the same task more gently. The fabric becomes smoother and brighter, while less water and energy are consumed.

Q24

解析 E段表明，某些酶能帮忙松动木质素，从而减少造纸时所需的含氯化学品（chemicals）的用量。

干扰 你可能会定位到chlorine compounds，但题目空格前已经写了chlorine-based，所以它对应的是原文后面的chlorine-based chemicals。

句子 Conventional bleaching can involve chlorine compounds, which may produce harmful pollutants if not carefully controlled. Certain enzymes can help loosen lignin or prepare the pulp for bleaching, reducing the amount of chlorine-based chemicals required.

Q25

解析 F段提到，研究人员通过把基因植入细菌或真菌，能把这些微生物变成大量生产商业用酶的微型工厂（factories）。

干扰 你的定位词应该是miniature（微型的），它后面的名词就是factories，别填成前面的bacteria这种干扰词。

句子 A further development combines enzymes with genetic engineering. Instead of simply finding useful enzymes in nature, researchers can insert selected genes into bacteria, yeasts or fungi, turning them into miniature factories. These organisms can then produce large quantities of enzymes for commercial use.

Q26

解析 I段清楚地说明，公司必须证明他们的新方法不会制造出新的风险（risks）。

干扰 题目中有“new”这个词，带着它回原文定位，就能直接锁定紧跟在它后面的“risks”。

句子 Regulation varies from country to country, and companies must prove that their methods do not create new risks. Nevertheless, the direction of travel is clear. The third wave of biotechnology is moving from the laboratory into everyday industry, and its influence may become visible not in what consumers buy, but in how those products are made.
